clue.text: Coming along with something attractive

definitions.meaning: going to get something and bringing it back with you
charming or pretty to look at

explanation.definitionFit: To go and bring something back is to fetch it, and a fetching outfit is a pretty, appealing one.

clue.text: Ladies' wear filled with stone

parts.note: women's dresses whose name has a stone, a rock, sitting inside it between F and S

explanation.surface: Women's clothing weighed down with pebbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The rock sits inside the word for these dresses; the outer F and S have no clue words of their own, so this is a cryptic hint, not full wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: These are women's dresses, a classic item of ladies' wear.

clue.text: A period of leisure, but not for the hangman

definitions.text: A period of leisure, but not for the hangman

parts.words: A period of leisure, but not for the hangman
parts.note: spare hours with nothing to do; for an executioner, the phrase would be literal work

explanation.surface: A remark that the executioner never gets a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for idle hours, read literally, describes the hangman's working moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means spare hours with nothing in particular to fill them.

clue.text: Elevated way of shopping, traditionally

parts.note: a lofty road read literally, and also the main road where shops are in a British town

explanation.surface: A raised route for going to the shops, as of old.
explanation.walkthrough: A HIGH STREET is the main shopping street of a British town; 'Elevated' gives HIGH and 'way' STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: The main road of a British town, lined with shops, is where people have traditionally gone shopping.

clue.text: Courageous prey?

definitions.meaning: wild animals hunted for sport or food

explanation.surface: A brave hunted animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucky person is up for anything, and wild animals shot for sport are the hunter's quarry.

clue.text: With a lot of these jewels, become very valuable!

definitions.text: With a lot of these jewels, become very valuable!

parts.words: With a lot of these jewels, become very valuable!
parts.note: the units used to weigh gems: the more of them a stone has, the more it is worth

explanation.surface: A remark that piling up plenty of gemstones makes you rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'these' are not jewels themselves but the measure of a jewel's weight; a stone of many of them is precious.
explanation.definitionFit: Gem weights are given in these units, so a high count means a heavy and costly stone.

clue.text: A loving touch worries, up to a point

indicators.note: up to in a down clue says the worries sit on top of the point

parts.note: cares are worries
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A tender touch soothes one's anxieties, to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to a point' looks like 'somewhat'; in a down clue CARES is placed above S, the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle stroke given with affection is a tender touch.

clue.text: Ferret in and around part of the eye

indicators.note: around says the answer lies about these words, spread across them

explanation.surface: A ferret poking in and around the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'Ferret in and'; 'in' is part of the text, not the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eyeball is one of its parts.

clue.text: Nigel's out for one at cricket

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

parts.note: read as Nigel plus S

explanation.surface: Nigel, the batsman, has been dismissed after scoring one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like cricket's dismissal, but it signals the anagram of NIGELS.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a run scored by one stroke is called by this word meaning one.

clue.text: A battle is remembered, in the long run

definitions.meaning: the Greek victory over Persia in 490 BC, fought on a plain near Athens

explanation.surface: Someone saying a famous fight will be recalled eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the long run' reads as the idiom 'eventually', but 'long run' is the second definition: the race named after the runner who carried news of the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek plain gave its name both to the 490 BC battle and to the 26-mile race commemorating the messenger's run.

clue.text: Riches he distributed to get a largish piece of England!

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are dealt out and spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A wealthy man shares out his money and in return gets a big chunk of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges RICHES and HE into the county name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sizeable county of north-west England, famous for its cheese and its grinning cat.

clue.text: Gets carried away?

parts.note: becomes overexcited, or literally is transported somewhere on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone who becomes overexcited.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for losing self-control is read literally: being carried along as a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling on a horse or a bus is being transported somewhere.

clue.text: One with a rash is seen

definitions.meaning: covered in red marks, as a person with a rash is

explanation.surface: A remark that someone with a skin complaint has been noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash leaves the skin marked with dots, and to catch sight of someone is also to have noticed them.

clue.text: Firm established for animal protection

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: a building set up to shelter horses

explanation.surface: A company that has been founded to look after animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a noun meaning a company, but it is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steady is secure, and a building that houses horses is their shelter.

clue.text: Showed his mettle, so to speak, but not solid enough for the Iron Duke

definitions.text: Showed his mettle, so to speak, but not solid enough for the Iron Duke

parts.words: Showed his mettle, so to speak, but not solid enough for the Iron Duke
parts.note: a toy fighter made of metal, punning mettle and metal, too flimsy to serve Wellington

explanation.surface: A soldier proved brave but was not tough enough for Wellington's army.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Duke is the Duke of Wellington; the metal toy is no match for an iron general, and SOLID shuffled appears in SOLDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy figure of a fighting man cast in metal.

clue.text: Book a cheerless dwelling

definitions.meaning: a Dickens novel about the Jarndyce lawsuit

explanation.surface: A gloomy house described in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens novel's title literally names a dismal, gloomy home.

clue.text: They pass through the mind, turning aside

indicators.note: turning means the letters of the next word are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: Thoughts that drift through one's head and then veer off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges the five letters of ASIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts and notions are what occur to us and pass through our heads.

clue.text: Money for the church writer first

indicators.note: first says the writer's letters come before the church's letters

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A collection for the church, the writer giving first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts PEN ahead of CE, reversing the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small British coins, a hundred of them to the pound.

clue.text: A real spread! Yet usually only part of a snack

definitions.text: A real spread! Yet usually only part of a snack

parts.words: A real spread! Yet usually only part of a snack
parts.note: a smooth meat or fish spread for sandwiches, while the same word means fake gems, so not real

explanation.surface: A lavish feast that is really only a light bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A real spread' sounds like a feast but means a genuine sandwich filling; the word also names imitation jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth savoury spread on bread is typically one part of a sandwich.

clue.text: Is courteous-but gets stick about it!

indicators.note: about means the stick's letters go round the next word

parts.note: a pole is a long stick
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who is perfectly courteous yet gets beaten for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is only a link; 'gets stick' suggests a beating, but the stick is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Being courteous means having good manners, which is a synonym for this adjective.

clue.text: Often mimics a flier

definitions.meaning: repeats what others say without thought
a bright tropical bird known for copying speech

explanation.surface: A bird that frequently imitates.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating words mindlessly is copying, as the talking tropical bird does.

clue.text: One Easterner in, and one out

definitions.text: One Easterner in, and one out

parts.words: One Easterner in, and one out
parts.note: a person from the subcontinent, and also a Native American, a westerner, out of the East

explanation.surface: One person from the East enters while another leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word names someone from the subcontinent and, by Columbus's mistake, a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from India is an Easterner; Columbus's mistaken name for Native Americans uses the same word.

clue.text: Being joyful, some made tales up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from the bottom upwards
some says only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Happy at heart, someone invented stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes DETALE from 'made tales' and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling great joy is the state of being thrilled and in high spirits.

clue.text: Badly surprised by the force of the current, maybe

definitions.meaning: startled or upset by something unexpected

definitions.text: by the force of the current, maybe
definitions.meaning: jolted by electricity running through the body

explanation.surface: Someone getting an unpleasant surprise from an electrical fault.
explanation.definitionFit: An upsetting surprise jolts you, and an electric current through the body gives the same kind of jolt.

clue.text: Shed is rebuilt for the convenience of those who eat

definitions.text: the convenience of those who eat

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters are put together again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A shed is reconstructed to make a handy dining area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges SHED and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates and bowls are what diners use to eat from, a convenience at table.

clue.text: Body-snatching resulting in this total failure?

definitions.text: Body-snatching resulting in this total failure?

parts.words: Body-snatching resulting in this total failure?
parts.note: a stolen corpse means a deceased person has gone missing, which is also a phrase for a complete flop

explanation.surface: Grave-robbers whose scheme ends in complete disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, snatching a body loses a corpse; the phrase is also an idiom for something useless.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person or venture that is utterly useless, a complete flop.

clue.text: Poet rose, the very opposite of brights

indicators.note: rose in a down clue means climbed, so the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet's rose, quite unlike bright colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the flower, but it is the verb: BARD climbs upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull, dreary colours are the contrast to bright ones.

clue.text: It's cooler at the front of the car-and warmer!

definitions.text: It's cooler at the front of the car
definitions.meaning: the engine-cooling grille unit behind a car's bonnet
the domestic heater fixed to a wall

explanation.surface: A remark about the cool air at the front of a car, and the heater too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' reads as 'colder', but it means the thing that cools the engine.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the device cooling a car engine and the wall heater in a house.

clue.text: Went about-though quite likely stayed in the same place

definitions.text: Went about-though quite likely stayed in the same place

parts.words: Went about-though quite likely stayed in the same place
parts.note: to go about is to face the other way, which can be done while standing still on one spot

explanation.surface: Someone who travelled around yet never really left home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went about' suggests travelling, but here it means spinning round to face the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating to face the other direction can be done on the spot, without moving anywhere.

clue.text: Obstacles to magical Peter's creator joining the Royal Society

parts.note: J M Barrie wrote Peter Pan
RS is the Royal Society, Britain's scientific academy

explanation.surface: Something blocking the author of Peter Pan from becoming a Fellow of the Royal Society.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstacles are things standing in your way, like fences or gates.
